your_life.name: Inspector Arun Mehra
your_life.recollections:
The district coat still carries the smell of the coach. Before the uniform there was Mill Lane: your father's wheel plane, your mother's account book, and Tara asking you to wait at the chapel turn. Twelve winters after her death, the institutional letter remains in your desk. You remember its careful wording.

Lewin kept the workshop clock running after your father died. Maela once copied a school certificate for Tara's friend. Ivo read a supposed message at a winter gathering you attended; you remember how the room responded, and the silence afterward. Tessa has written to you about ordinary clerical work for years.

You came back to Bhairav's Hollow on ordinary leave. The road is under snow, the lamps are lit, and people are still finishing the day's work.

place.name: Chapel scriptorium
place.description: A lamp burns beside the reading lectern. A cup and a small labelled bottle stand on a tray, where evening visitors leave their remedies before sitting down. On the keeper's desk lie dispensary papers and a sealed reference vial. Doors open toward the square and the quieter side hall. The bell rope hangs motionless beside the wall.

task.name: The Bell Before Dawn
task.scope: Investigate the death in the chapel and the apparently prophetic warning. Establish responsibility for the death, any fabrication of the warning document, and how it was relayed. Foreknowledge alone does not establish participation in a killing.
task.success: Support the death attribution, warning fabrication and its transmission with acquired sources. Unresolved supernatural explanations may remain explicit; they are not scored.

people.name: Maela Rowan
people.appearance: A woman in an ink-marked cuff keeps loose pages tied with blue thread.

people.name: Alba Reed
people.appearance: A chapel keeper has a pencil tied to the dispensary book with string.

findings.label: body
findings.description: Tessa Rowan lies beside the lectern, unresponsive after drinking, with no visible external injury.

findings.label: labelled tonic bottle
findings.description: The bottle still bears the mint-cordial label, but a dark residue marks the stopper and the liquid left inside.

findings.label: sealed reference vial
findings.description: A sealed reference vial contains the ordinary cordial, retained with its dispensing entry. The entry describes the fictional ironleaf preparation as a different, harmful dispensary material; no quantities or preparation instructions are given.

findings.label: dispensing record
findings.description: Alba recorded the cordial as clear before it left the dispensary. A retained-paper assay distinguishes it from the fictional ironleaf preparation, which leaves a dark stain.

observation.observation: The retained-paper assay described in the dispensing record distinguishes the bottle residue from the sealed ordinary cordial. In this fictional dispensary it matches ironleaf preparation, a harmful adulterant. This establishes adulteration, not who added it; no real-world toxicology or dosage claim is made.

recollections.text: The sealed reference vial and dispensing record are on my desk.
Maela Rowan arrives from Chapel side hall.
Maela Rowan opens the tonic bottle and mixes in a dark preparation before replacing the stopper.
Tessa Rowan arrives from The lamp-lit square.
Tessa Rowan drinks the cordial from the labelled bottle.
Tessa Rowan collapses beside the lectern after drinking. No one gives a medical explanation at this moment.

place.name: Chapel side hall
place.description: Two writing tables stand beneath the coat hooks. One is used by Maela for hospital copies; the other holds Lewin's repair accounts. The chapel and square can both be reached from here. A parcel shelf catches paper scraps that the stove has not yet claimed.

findings.label: paper offcut
findings.description: An unused offcut has an uneven toothed tear.

findings.label: signed account
findings.description: An ordinary account signed in full by Maela Rowan. Its lettering is closely spaced, with a double stroke on the final letter.

findings.label: paper offcut
findings.description: An unused offcut has a straight trimmed edge.

findings.label: signed account
findings.description: An ordinary account signed in full by Lewin Crowe. Its lettering is broad and upright.

place.name: The lamp-lit square
place.description: Snow has collected against the chapel steps. Across the road the inn keeps a line of light under its door. The chapel side hall opens beside a covered passage. Voices travel across the square more easily than faces can be made out.

place.name: Pine Lantern common room
place.description: The stove has gathered a small audience who pretend not to be listening to one another. A notice board stands beside the counter, and the lodging desk has a clock that gains a minute each winter. The square is outside. Someone has pinned a narrow sheet under a warning about the road.

people.name: Ivo Lark
people.appearance: A reader holds a folded scarf against his chest and chooses his words slowly.

people.name: Niv Soren
people.appearance: A young runner has melted snow on the shoulders of his coat.

findings.label: warning letter
findings.description: “Before the last bell, Tessa will fall beside her reading lamp. The old bell keeper has spoken.” The paper has a toothed torn edge. The close lettering has a double stroke on its final letters.

findings.label: delivery docket
findings.description: Niv’s docket records a sealed paper delivered to Ivo at the inn before Tessa entered the chapel. The inn clock time was countersigned by the recipient.

recollections.text: I keep delivery dockets at the lodging desk after the evening round.
Maela Rowan gives a folded sheet to Niv Soren for delivery to Ivo at the inn.
Niv Soren arrives from Chapel side hall.
Niv Soren arrives from The lamp-lit square.
Niv Soren delivers the folded warning to Ivo Lark before the chapel visit.
Ivo Lark repeats the warning from the delivered sheet and presents it as a message from the old bell keeper.

observation.observation: The warning sheet and unused offcut have matching toothed tears, with fibres continuing across the join. Paper ownership alone does not establish authorship. The warning’s close lettering and doubled final strokes agree with the independently signed account.
